Until further notice, derived L1 pCO2 data products from this sensor are incorrect and should not be used. A significant discrepancy has been uncovered between the pCO2 values from shipboard water samples vs. values calculated by OOI system. The pco2_pco2wat algorithm is under review and can be viewed at https://github.com/ooici/ion-functions/blob/master/ion_functions/data/co2_functions.py. To receive instant notification of updates to the code, add yourself as a watcher to the GitHub repository linked above. For further questions please email help@oceanobservatories.org.

Note: On Thursday, January 26th, the Shallow Profiler at Axial Base (SC03A) stopped during the profiler down cast. Analysis of the data indicates the Science Pod (SciP) turned around (commenced down cast profiles) below its normal ceiling due to wave action. Investigation of the engineering data revealed the EM cable is tangled on the drum. The current depth of the SciP is approximately 50m below the surface. The Science Pod is powered and science/engineering data continued to be collected.

Analog output from the optodes is produced by using a digital to analog converter (DAC). DAC configuration was initially only done at power up or reset, but firmware version 4.6.4 began updating configuration each time the analog output value was updated to ensure long-term continuous operation. Unfortunately, this also produced a voltage jump, creating erratic noise in the output data. The firmware has been corrected, but only the onboard-calculated Stern-Volmer values [DO from Onboard Calculation (L1 product; 'ctd_tc_oxygen') and DO from Onboard Calculation - Corrected (L2 product; 'dissolved_oxygen')] should be used during this annotated time range, NOT the 'DO from Phase' data which contain the noisy analog signal.

In April 2026 HITL review showed that the shallow profiler platform experienced an unprecedented major blowdown event (~40 m deep) lasting over a month, most likely due to strong eddy currents. Temperature, oxygen, and pH are all well below historical values, and other parameters are also anomalous during this time period.
